cycles.method: static: tools/build/cycle_count.py (--verify: the marker is a no-op), the per-sample loop with the bucket tick taken, 401 cycles/sample. measured: perf.py bench, benchmark_reverbs.run as benchmark_stock_dsp.py runs it (one instance per core at positions 0 and 4, audio at X:0, 4,096 blocks of 16 frames, the null stub's peak subtracted) on a private native image carrying BBD in SPRING REV's space (ffe65ea1..., BBD14). Worst of 46 BBD cases: the moving-knob pattern with a trig split, 433.31 executed instructions/sample (406.38 unsplit). Executed instructions in dsp_host, not chip cycles; no stalls modelled.

stock.baseline: perf.py bench: SPRING REV, CHORUS and DJ EQ run on the stock image through the same cases as BBD (fixed, the moving pattern, a trig split at every position 1-15). Its unsplit figures reproduce out/stock_dsp_bench/results.json exactly (SPRING REV 257.5, CHORUS 253.62, DJ EQ 293.38).
stock.justification: BBD runs a whole bucket-brigade chain per sample: a 2:1 feedback compressor whose divide (24 steps, the Pade tanh folded in) runs every sample, an 8th-order Butterworth anti-alias and a 7th + 2nd order reconstruction filter (eight biquads and a real pole, about 90 words of the loop) that track the clock, the clocked bucket line with a charge-transfer polynomial and noise, a DC blocker, the expander, the feedback tilt (a split and a bandpass) and a soft output stage. Under the same cases, trig splits included, its worst case 433.31 is 1.48x CHORUS (293.06, the closest stock effect: a BBD-style modulated line), 1.38x SPRING REV (314.19, the cost target for new FX) and 1.31x DJ EQ (330.94, the dearest stock effect); unsplit 406.38 against 253.62, 257.50 and 293.38. Moving FDBK and TONE glides to once a call saved 23 static cycles (368 to 345, before FRZ, LIM, the MIX curve and PRE/POST brought the loop to 415; a bookkeeping pass with bit-identical output then took it to 402; BBD13's FRZ removed the per-bucket mix, 401), and rotating one filter section per call instead of all nine took the per-call coefficient work from ten divides to two. Going further means lower filter orders, which changes the sound. Four per core are 4 x 401 = 1,604 of the 3,120 usable static cycles. That leaves 1,516 for the four FX1 effects on those tracks and any other module on the core; the stress run with CHORUS on every FX1 peaked at 2,802.4 executed instructions per sample per core. Real-chip headroom beside heavy FX1 effects is unmeasured: hardware untested. The worst case has the SETUP high-passes PRE and POST on (two fixed 150 Hz 2-pole Butterworth sections, about 25 cycles each); both are branched around when OFF, their default, where the fixed-knob case measures 370.38 (a 5,993-instruction peak block less the 67-instruction null stub, over 16 frames).

stress.method: perf.py stress (E-Verb's load, adapted). stress_project.py needs an Octatrack template project, which is not available here, so the same load is driven straight into dsp_host on the private native image (BBD14, ffe65ea1...): BBD on FX2 of all eight tracks (four per core) behind CHORUS on every FX1 (eight named slots; DJ EQ, the dearest stock effect, has five); per block, three LFOs (sine, triangle, square) on BBD's TIME, FDBK and MIX, and a new random value on every named slot of both effects each sixteenth at 120 BPM: 18 slots changed per step, of which 12 can be locked on a unit (BBD's six main-page knobs and CHORUS's six; STGS, LIM, PRE, POST and CHORUS's TAPS and FBLP are SETUP knobs that change only with Parts on a unit, so this changes more than locks can, repeatedly forces BBD's fade-and-clear and switches PRE and POST); trig splits of 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 15 frames on six tracks; eight different 32 s stems plus a 2 s tail; dsp_host -guard 0x4000 -guard-shared -dirty 0x5a. Result: no hang; BBD's eight instances 0 stray writes and 0 clobbers, and no instance clobbers another (the guard also counts 13318840 stray-write regions for the stock CHORUS instances, not examined further); per-core peak 2774.8 and 2802.4 executed instructions/sample with all sixteen effects. It exercises the DSP side only: the firmware's own LFO and lock delivery, Part switches and the ColdFire side are not in it.
